newsitem.title: UK: INSTANT VIEW-Political analysts comment on UK poll.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW-Political analysts comment on UK poll.

text.p: Following is a selection of comments from political analysts on the outcome of Britain's May 1 parliamentary election, made as results were announced.
0100 GMT -- ANTHONY KING, PROFESSOR OF GOVERNMENT AT THE UNIVERSITY OF ESSEX
"There is really a fundamental change in the structure of the British political system. Here is the unionist party being driven out of important parts of the union (Scotland and Wales)."
"There is enormous tactical voting on behalf of (Labour and the Liberal Democrats) and the Conservatives are simply being squeezed."
"They (the Tories) are down to their worst figure in this century by a wide margin".
0038 GMT -- MICHAEL THRASHER, PROFESSOR OF POLITICS AT PLYMOUTH UNIVERSITY (after third-placed Liberal Democrats took seven seats)
"It really does look as though a Liberal Democrat tide is going to sweep across the south-west."

(On other results) "There are huge amounts of swing around which we normally associate with local elections, not (parliamentary) elections." ('Swing' measures the size of change of the vote from one party to another since the 1992 parliamentary election).
0018 GMT -- IVOR CREWE, VICE-CHANCELLOR AT THE UNIVERSITY OF ESSEX (after Putney result)

"David Mellor is the second ex-Conservative cabinet minister to fall. Sir James Goldsmith only got 1,500 votes, far less than people were expecting. A very disappointing result for the Referendum Party."
2348 GMT - BOB WORCESTER, CHAIRMAN OF MORI POLLING ORGANISATION (after 15 percent swing to Labour in Basildon, in Essex, a constituency seen as a barometer of 1980s Conservatism)

"A key result in the 1992 election was the winning of Essex man in Basildon. That was a triumph of the Conservative party becasue it meant that John Major, against the polls, was winning that election. But Essex man is dead."

"The BBC poll is now talking about a 203 (-seat) majority overall for the Labour party -- the worst showing of 18.2 (share of the vote) for the Conservative party and the best showing from the Labour party ever in its history," Worcester told CNN.
